# Job Chapter 17 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 422r–422v

---

**17:1** "My-spirit [ruchi] is-broken [chubbalah], my-days [yamai] are-extinguished [niz'aku], the-graveyard [qevarim] [is] mine [li].

**17:2** Surely [im lo] mockeries [hatulim] [are] with-me [immadi], and-on-their-provocations [behammeroatam] my-eye [eini] lodges [talen].

**17:3** Set-down [simah] now, be-my-pledge [orevni] with-you [immakh]; who [is] he [who] to-my-hand [leyadi] will-strike [yittaqe'a]?

**17:4** For their-heart [libbam] you-have-hidden [tsafanta] from understanding [missekhel]; therefore [al ken] you-will-not exalt-them [teromem].

**17:5** For-a-share [le-cheleq] he-declares [yaggid] friends [re'im], and-the-eyes of-his-sons [benav] will-fail [tiklena].

**17:6** And-he-has-set-me [vehitsigani] as-a-byword [limshal] of-the-peoples [ammim], and-a-spitting [vetofe] in-the-face [lefanim] I-have-become [ehyeh].

**17:7** And-my-eye [eini] is-dim [vatekhah] from-grief [mikka'as], and-my-limbs [yetsuray] [are] like-a-shadow [katsel] all-of-them [kullam].

**17:8** The-upright [yesharim] are-appalled [yashommu] at this, and-the-innocent [naqi] against the-godless [chanef] rouses-himself [yit'orar].

**17:9** And-the-righteous [tsaddiq] holds [yachaz] to-his-way [darkho], and-the-clean of-hands [utehor yadayim] adds [yosif] strength [omets].

**17:10** But-indeed [ve-ulam] all-of-you, turn [shuvu] and-come [uvo'u] now; and-I-will-not find [ve-lo emtsa] among-you a-wise-one [chacham].

**17:11** My-days [yamai] have-passed [averu], my-plans [zimotai] are-torn-apart [nitteshu], the-desires [morashei] of-my-heart [levavi].

**17:12** Night [lailah] they-set [yasimu] as-day [la-yom]; light [or] [is] near [qarov] before [mippenei] darkness [choshekh].

**17:13** If I-wait [aqavveh], Sheol [she'ol] [is] my-house [beiti]; in-the-darkness [bachoshekh] I-spread [rippadeti] my-couch [yetsu'ai].

**17:14** To-the-pit [lashshachat] I-call [qarati], 'My-father [avi] [are] you'; 'My-mother [immi] and-my-sister [achoti]' — to-the-worm [larimmah].

**17:15** And-where [ve-ayyeh] then [efo] [is] my-hope [tiqvati]? And-my-hope [vetiqvati] — who will-see-it [yeshurenah]?

**17:16** [To] the-bars [baddei] of-Sheol [she'ol] they-will-go-down [teradna]; if [im] together [yachad] upon the-dust [al afar] [there is] rest [nachat]."

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — "the graveyard is mine":** A stark claim of ownership — the only thing Job possesses anymore is his grave. The Hebrew *qevarim* is plural, intensifying the image.

**v.3 — "be my pledge":** Job asks God to post bail for him — to stand as his own guarantor, since no human will. The legal language (*arav*, "pledge/surety") continues the courtroom metaphor.

**v.14 — "Father... Mother... Sister":** Job addresses the pit and the worm with kinship terms. Death has become his family. This is among the most desolate images in the Hebrew Bible — Job's only remaining relatives are decay and corruption.

**v.9 — "the righteous holds to his way":** This verse has puzzled commentators — it seems to interrupt Job's despair with a statement of conventional piety. Some read it as ironic; others as a brief assertion that the truly righteous can face Job's situation without abandoning integrity.

*— EMET*
